editorial:
If you like weird horror with dark laughs, Tusk is a wild ride. The story follows Wallace, a podcast host who travels to Canada and disappears after meeting a strange old man. His best friend Teddy and girlfriend Ally team up to find him, but what they discover is far stranger than a missing person case. The movie mixes silly podcast humor with body horror, so it feels like a campfire story told by someone who loves gross-out jokes. It is not for everyone, but if you enjoy oddball movies that commit fully to a bizarre idea, you will probably have a good time.

The acting is energetic, especially Justin Long as Wallace and Michael Parks as the creepy Howard. The pacing moves quickly once the search begins, and the walrus transformation is unforgettable. The movie can feel mean-spirited and the humor will not land for every viewer, but the commitment to its strange concept is impressive. Watch it if you want something different and do not mind gross scenes. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Wallace is fully transformed into a walrus and kept in a tank by Howard. Teddy and Ally finally track him down, but Howard attacks and is killed during the struggle. Wallace survives as a walrus, no longer able to speak or live as a human. The movie ends with Teddy and Ally visiting him, showing he still recognizes them in some small way, leaving a sad and strange final image.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird horror comedies and cult movies.
